objective_name: Cells as the Basic Unit of Life

questions.prompt: Which statement is true about all living things?

answer_choices.D: They are made of water only.

questions.explanation: All living things are made of one or more cells. Cells are the basic unit of life.

questions.prompt: A bacterium is made of only one cell. A bacterium is:
questions.explanation: An organism made of one cell is unicellular. Many bacteria are unicellular organisms.

questions.prompt: Which organism is multicellular?
questions.explanation: Humans are made of many cells, so they are multicellular. Bacteria, amoebas, and paramecia are examples of unicellular organisms.

questions.prompt: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.explanation: A cell is the basic unit of life. All living things are made of one or more cells.

questions.prompt: An organism made of many cells is called:
questions.explanation: A multicellular organism is made of many cells. Humans, trees, and mushrooms are examples of multicellular organisms.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a unicellular organism?

answer_choices.A: It is made of many tissues.
answer_choices.B: It is made of one cell.
answer_choices.D: It is made only of organs.

questions.explanation: A unicellular organism is made of one cell. That one cell carries out the functions needed for life.

questions.prompt: Which object is nonliving?
questions.explanation: A rock is nonliving because it is not made of cells. Bacteria, mushrooms, and trees are living things made of cells.

questions.prompt: A student observes an organism under a microscope and sees only one cell. How should the organism be classified?
questions.explanation: If an organism consists of only one cell, it is classified as unicellular.

questions.prompt: A diagram shows a tree, a dog, a mushroom, and a rock. Which object is NOT made of cells?
questions.explanation: Trees, dogs, and mushrooms are living things and are made of cells. Rocks are nonliving and are not made of cells.

questions.prompt: Scientists observe four organisms. Organism A contains 1 cell. Organism B contains 50 cells. Organism C contains 1,000 cells. Organism D contains 10,000 cells. Which organism is unicellular?
questions.explanation: A unicellular organism is made of only one cell. Organism A contains a single cell, so it is unicellular.

questions.prompt: A student compares a dog, a mushroom, and a rock. Which statement correctly classifies them?

answer_choices.A: The dog and mushroom are living because they are made of cells.
answer_choices.B: Only the dog is living because mushrooms do not move.
answer_choices.C: The rock is living because it is found outside.
answer_choices.D: All three are living because they are natural objects.

questions.explanation: Dogs and mushrooms are living things made of cells. A rock is natural, but it is not living because it is not made of cells.

questions.prompt: An organism is observed and found to contain only one cell. What is the best classification for this organism?
questions.explanation: An organism made of only one cell is unicellular. Being made of one cell does not mean it is nonliving.

questions.prompt: A teacher shows students two examples: an amoeba made of one cell and a human made of many cells. What do both examples have in common?
questions.explanation: Both amoebas and humans are living things made of cells. An amoeba is unicellular, while a human is multicellular.

questions.prompt: A sample contains many different types of cells working together. What can be concluded about the organism?

answer_choices.D: It is made of only one cell.

questions.explanation: An organism with many cells, especially different types of cells, is multicellular.

questions.prompt: A student claims that mushrooms are not living things because they do not move from place to place. Which evidence best refutes the student's claim?
questions.explanation: One characteristic of living things is that they are made of cells. The presence of cells is stronger evidence that mushrooms are living than their color or location.

questions.prompt: Two organisms are observed. Organism A contains one cell. Organism B contains many cells. What conclusion can be made?

answer_choices.A: Organism A is living and Organism B is nonliving.
answer_choices.B: Organism A is unicellular and Organism B is multicellular.

questions.explanation: A single-celled organism is unicellular. An organism made of many cells is multicellular. Both can be living organisms.

questions.prompt: A student claims that only animals are made of cells. Which evidence best shows that the claim is incorrect?

answer_choices.B: Plants can be observed to have cells.

questions.explanation: The strongest evidence is that plants have cells. This shows that animals are not the only living things made of cells.

questions.prompt: Two samples are observed. Sample A contains cells. Sample B does not contain cells. Which conclusion is best supported?

answer_choices.A: Sample A may be living, while Sample B is nonliving.
answer_choices.B: Sample B must be living because it has no cells.

questions.explanation: Living things are made of cells. If Sample B has no cells, it is not living. If Sample A contains cells, it may be living or may have come from something living.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why both bacteria and humans are considered living organisms?

answer_choices.A: Both are made of cells, even though bacteria have one cell and humans have many.
answer_choices.B: Both are made of many organs.
answer_choices.C: Both are always visible without tools.
answer_choices.D: Both have the same number of cells.

questions.explanation: Both bacteria and humans are living because both are made of cells. Bacteria are unicellular, while humans are multicellular.

questions.prompt: A student says, “If something does not move from place to place, it must not be alive.” Which example best shows why this reasoning is incorrect?

answer_choices.A: A rock does not move and is not alive.
answer_choices.B: A tree does not move from place to place but is made of cells.
answer_choices.C: A cloud moves but is not made of cells.
answer_choices.D: A car moves but is not alive.

questions.explanation: Movement from place to place is not required for something to be alive. A tree is living because it is made of cells, even though it does not move from place to place.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by the idea that cells are the basic unit of life?

answer_choices.A: All living things must be made of one or more cells.
answer_choices.B: Only large organisms are made of cells.
answer_choices.C: Nonliving things become alive when they move.

questions.explanation: If cells are the basic unit of life, then all living things must be made of one or more cells. Some living things have one cell, while others have many.
